A.title: Null normal pairs and screen geometry
A.statement: On a smooth spacelike closed two-surface S in an oriented time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, choose future null normals l,k with g(l,k)=-2. Define q as the positive induced metric, chi_l(X,Y)=g(nabla_X l,Y), theta_l=tr_q chi_l and sigma_l=chi_l-(theta_l/2)q. Rescaling l by exp(f) and k by exp(-f) is a normal-frame boost.
A.proof_route: Construct the rank-two normal bundle locally; give overlap boost laws and prove q is positive. No global choice of normal frame is inferred without a stated trivialization.

A.title: Null Raychaudhuri and conjugate-point bound
A.statement: For a twist-free affinely parametrized null geodesic hypersurface congruence in four dimensions, before its first caustic, dtheta/dlambda=-theta^2/2-|sigma|^2-Ric(l,l). If Ric(l,l)>=0 and theta(0)<0, a focal point occurs by affine length 2/|theta(0)| provided the generators exist that long.
A.proof_route: Derive the screen Riccati equation from the Jacobi equation, take its trace, and integrate (1/theta)' >=1/2 while theta<0. Prove the Jacobi determinant vanishes when the expansion blows down; do not infer curvature blowup.

A.title: Null focal points exclude later horismos generators
A.statement: Let S be a smooth spacelike two-surface and gamma a future affinely parametrized normal null geodesic. A focal instant is a positive lambda at which a nonzero normal-screen Jacobi variation with initial point varying in S and initial screen derivative chi_l has zero screen value. If a focal instant occurs at lambda0, then gamma(lambda) lies in I^+(S) for every sufficiently close lambda>lambda0, and hence the generator cannot remain in E^+(S) beyond that instant.
A.proof_route: Write the null screen index form with the S boundary term determined by chi_l. A focal Jacobi field gives a zero index direction up to lambda0. Extend by zero and add a small smooth screen perturbation supported across lambda0; integration by parts at the derivative jump makes the index form strictly negative. Construct the corresponding variation with starting point on S; use a small longitudinal null correction to obtain a timelike curve to a point just beyond the focal instant. The local convex-normal cone criterion and push-up turn this into chronological membership. This complete null second-variation argument must be authored; the retained timelike maximum theorem is not substituted.

A.statement: Let Sigma be a closed smooth three-manifold, htilde a smooth Riemannian metric, tau a real constant, sigmatilde a smooth transverse-traceless covariant tensor and Lambda=0. pairs.title: Covariant phase space and boundary ambiguities

A.title: Covariant presymplectic current
A.statement: Let L be a smooth local four-form Lagrangian for fields phi on an oriented four-manifold and let a chosen variational decomposition be delta L=E(phi) dot delta phi+d theta(phi;delta phi). For commuting smooth variations define omega(phi;delta1 phi,delta2 phi)=delta2 theta(phi;delta1 phi)-delta1 theta(phi;delta2 phi). For a compact oriented three-surface Sigma put Omega_Sigma=integral_Sigma omega.
A.proof_route: Use Iyer-Wald ordering explicitly. Define variations as derivatives of a smooth two-parameter family, so commutation and passage through d/integrals have a stated regularity basis.

A.title: On-shell closure and finite-region symplectic flux
A.statement: If E=0 and both variations obey delta_i E=0, then d omega=0. For a compact region with oriented boundary Sigma2-Sigma1+B, Omega_Sigma2-Omega_Sigma1=-integral_B omega.
A.proof_route: Antisymmetrize the two variations of L: d omega=delta1 E dot delta2 phi-delta2 E dot delta1 phi under the chosen ordering. Apply finite-region Stokes. Cauchy independence requires zero boundary flux, not on-shell closure alone.

A.title: Potential ambiguity is a corner term
A.statement: Replacing L by L+d mu and theta by theta+delta mu+dY changes omega by d(delta2 Y(delta1)-delta1 Y(delta2)); the delta mu terms cancel. Consequently Omega on a compact surface changes by the corresponding integral over its boundary.
A.proof_route: Commute variations, use delta_i d=d delta_i and surface Stokes. A boundary condition may kill the corner term; covariance alone does not.

A.title: Admissible reduction and Hamiltonian generators
A.statement: On a specified solution space with specified admissible variations and boundary conditions, call Omega presymplectic if it is closed but possibly degenerate. A reduced symplectic manifold exists only when the null distribution has a smooth quotient with a descended nondegenerate two-form. A Hamiltonian for an admissible vector field X satisfies i_X Omega=dH on that specified space.
A.proof_route: Use the existing finite-dimensional reduction only for tangent linear models; it does not establish an infinite-dimensional smooth quotient. The library convention i_XH omega=dH fixes bracket signs.

pairs.title: Tetrads, Lorentz connections and spin interfaces

A.title: Local Lorentz tetrad and connection
A.statement: On a trivializing patch let e^I be a smooth coframe, eta=diag(-1,1,1,1), g=eta_IJ e^I tensor e^J and omega^I_J an so(1,3)-valued one-form. Define torsion T^I=de^I+omega^I_J wedge e^J and curvature F^I_J=domega^I_J+omega^I_K wedge omega^K_J. Under eprime=Lambda e put omegaprime=Lambda omega Lambda^-1-dLambda Lambda^-1.
A.proof_route: A local coframe need not extend globally. Distinguish a Lorentz connection from a spin lift; the title is an interface and not an assertion that a spin structure exists.

A.title: Torsion-free tetrad equivalence to Levi-Civita
A.statement: For a nondegenerate coframe there is exactly one eta-skew connection one-form with de^I+omega^I_J wedge e^J=0; its induced tangent connection is the metric-selected torsion-free connection. Under a Lorentz coframe change Fprime=Lambda F Lambda^-1 and Tprime=Lambda T.
A.proof_route: Construct omega from the existing Levi-Civita connection in the frame. Conversely the Cartan torsion equation implies zero tangent torsion and eta-skewness gives metric compatibility; uniqueness follows from Levi-Civita. Expand the gauge law to cancel dLambda terms.

A.title: Lorentzian spin-lift interface
A.statement: For an oriented time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, a Lorentzian spin structure is a principal Spin+(1,3) bundle with an equivariant double-cover map to the oriented time-oriented orthonormal SO+(1,3) frame bundle. The chosen spin representation gives its associated complex spinor bundle, and a lifted Lorentz connection differentiates spinors. This definition assumes a supplied smooth double cover and a chosen lift; it asserts neither lift existence nor uniqueness.
A.proof_route: Define Spin+(1,3) concretely via SL(2,C) acting on Hermitian 2x2 matrices X=x0 I+x dot sigma by X->A X A dagger; det X=x0^2-|x|^2. Prove kernel {+I,-I}, local differential isomorphism and surjectivity onto the identity component before using the cover.

A.title: Local spin-connection Clifford compatibility
A.statement: For gamma matrices with {gamma^I,gamma^J}=2eta^IJ I and omega_IJ=-omega_JI, the local spin covariant derivative D=d+(1/4)omega_IJ gamma^I gamma^J induces the vector Lorentz connection under Clifford multiplication. The assertion is local and presumes the selected spin representation.
A.proof_route: Compute [gamma^I gamma^J,gamma^K]=2(eta^JK gamma^I-eta^IK gamma^J) and contract with omega_IJ. Fix raised/lowered gamma conventions before identifying the vector action.

A.title: Connection transport and endpoint gauge action
A.statement: For a C^1 path gamma:[0,1]->U and continuous matrix-valued omega(gammadot), define transport U_gamma as the endpoint solution Udot=-omega(gammadot)U, U(0)=I. Concatenation is piecewise C^1 with its orientation stated; reversal reverses the path.
A.proof_route: Use linear ODE existence and uniqueness for finite-dimensional matrices. This defines tangent/associated-bundle transport, not foliation holonomy.

A.title: Transport composition and gauge covariance
A.statement: Transport obeys U_(gamma2*gamma1)=U_gamma2 U_gamma1, U_(gamma^-1)=U_gamma^-1, and under eprime=Lambda e, Uprime_gamma=Lambda(gamma(1)) U_gamma Lambda(gamma(0))^-1.
A.proof_route: Solve separately on concatenated pieces and invoke uniqueness. Differentiate Lambda(gamma(t))U(t)Lambda(gamma(0))^-1 and substitute the connection transformation law. The resulting path groupoid functor need not factor through the fundamental groupoid unless curvature vanishes.

A.title: Curvature controls infinitesimal loop transport
A.statement: For a C^2 matrix connection on a coordinate rectangle based at p with side lengths epsilon in directions i then j, traversed in positive boundary order, U_loop=I-epsilon^2 F_ij(p)+O(epsilon^3) in a fixed local frame.
A.proof_route: Expand the four segment ODE solutions through second order, including first derivatives of omega; multiplication yields -(partial_i omega_j-partial_j omega_i+[omega_i,omega_j])epsilon^2. Uniform C^2 bounds on a compact patch control the remainder.

A.title: A finite graph holonomy model
A.statement: For a finite oriented graph with compact group G=SU(2), assign g_e in G, g_reverse=g_e^-1; a vertex gauge transformation h_v acts by g_e->h_target g_e h_source^-1. A Wilson loop in a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation rho is tr rho(product of edge elements in path order). This is a finite configuration model, not an established continuum quantum theory of gravity.
A.proof_route: Define the graph, path ordering, representation and group before taking trace. Vertex gauge invariance follows by endpoint cancellation and trace cyclicity. The SU(2) choice requires a separate time-gauge reduction for a gravity interpretation.

A.title: Finite-vertex Haar projection onto invariant tensors
A.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite graph and prescribed finite-dimensional unitary edge representations of compact G=SU(2), form at each vertex the tensor product W_v of incoming representation spaces and outgoing dual representation spaces. The normalized Haar average P_v=integral_G R_v(g) dmu(g) is the orthogonal projection onto W_v^G. Products of these vertex projections impose the finite vertex gauge invariance condition on the graph coefficient tensor space; no Hamiltonian or continuum constraint is imposed.
A.proof_route: Apply the exact Haar intertwiner projection with H=C carrying the trivial representation, J=W_v and T(1)=w. Its contraction/idempotence gives an invariant-vector projection. If P is a contractive idempotent on a Hilbert space, take x in its range and y in its kernel, and compare ||x||^2<=||x+t y||^2 for real and imaginary t to get orthogonality. Distinct vertex gauge actions commute on edge coefficient factors, so their projections commute.
